Judgment

This is a charge sheet filed by the P.S.I of Rajarajeshwari Nagara P.S. against the accused No.1 to 3 for the offences punishable U/Sec.63 of Copy Right Act and 381 & 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
02.

The brief facts of the prosecution case is that, on 16.06.2014 at 4 pm., the accused No.1 came to sale the tins which are resembles to Ashirwad Company tins in Surya Seramic Shop situated at Rajarajeshwari Nagara.
At that time, the CW.2 & 4 caught him red handedly with the materials and cheated the company and public and thus the accused persons have committed the above said offences.
Prior to filing of charge sheet the accused No.1 & 3 are enlarged on bail in crime stage.
After filing of charge sheet, this court took cognizance for the offences punishable U/Sec.63 of Copy Right Act and 381 & 420 r/w 34 of IPC and issued summons to the accused No.1 & 3 only.
Accordingly the accused No.1 & 3 appeared before the court through their counsel.
The case against accused No.3 was split-up on 24.04.2023.

Later on, charge sheet copies and prosecution papers were furnished to the accused No.1 under Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.
04.
Heard both side on framing of charge, perused the prosecution papers.
As there are sufficient materials to frame the charge against the accused No.1, the charges has been framed and the same were read over to them, but he pleaded not guilty and claimed for trial.
Hence the case was posted for prosecution evidence.

05. The prosecution in order to prove its case has not examined any of the witnesses, in spite of repeated issuance of NBW against CW.1 to 10 the concerned agency failed to execute the same to the said witnesses and brought them before this court, hence prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected.
CW.1 to 10 were C.C.No.12313/2019 dropped and closed the side of the prosecution evidence, as there is no incriminating circumstances against the accused No.1.
Hence, the accused statement U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with and posted for judgment.

06. In order to prove the guilt of the offence as alleged against the accused No.1 by the prosecution,
the prosecution has not at all examined any one of the witnesses.
It is relevant to note that, the prosecution has cited 10 witnesses.
In spite of issuance of summons warrant against the CW.1 to CW.10, the prosecution has utterly failed to secure the presence of CW.1 to CW.10.

Though this Court issued coercive process of witness warrant against CW.1 to CW.10 and even recalled them,
they have not appeared before the court.
Therefore, this Court dropped out CW.1 to CW.10.
Therefore, this Court proceed in accordance with law.

Hence, prosecution has utterly failed to prove Balamurali Krishna vs Omprkaksh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27415428/
2 the guilt of the offence as alleged against the accused No.1 beyond reasonable doubt.

07.

Point No.2:- In view of the findings recorded to the above points, this court proceed to pass the following:-
C.C.No.12313/2019 ORDER

By exercising powers conferred U/sec. 248(1) of Cr.P.C.,
the accused No.1 is acquitted for the offences punishable U/Sec.63 of Copy Right Act and 381 & 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond of the accused No.1 shall continue in force for a period of 6 months.
The accused No.1 is set at liberty.
The properties mentioned in SL.No.1 & 2 of PF No.53/2014 are ordered to be destroyed as worthless after appeal period is over.
Office is hereby directed to preserve this case file till disposal of split CC.No.10169/2023 against accused No.2 & 3.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and print out taken by her is verified and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 8th day of September 2025.)
(Sri. Vinod Balnaik.)
IX Addl.Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
